Multi-instrumentalist, composer, and visual artist Roscoe Mitchell has been in the forefront of creative music since the late 1960s. He was a founding member of the Association for the Advancement of Creative Musicians and the Art Ensemble of Chicago. He has been honored for his work by numerous organizations including the National Endowment of the Arts.
Roscoe was interviewed via Zoom on May 23, 2023 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

I want to start out with an interesting quote I read in an interview you did in 1998. It’s very short, it says, “I have so many ideas that my head is exploding with ideas.” It must have been a productive time for you and I can relate to that because my head is exploding with questions. But I think I’ll just ask you first what are you currently working on, either visual art wise or music wise?

Everything. I mean you know I think that like people are going to want to see what people have been doing. I mean you know during this pandemic or whatever. So, and people are going to be looking for information you know. So I’m just doing whatever I can so that I’m prepared to meet the challenges that are going to be ahead.
That’s like a sort of a hopeful way of thinking that people are looking for information and hopefully ready to hear it and view it.
Yeah that is. I mean aren’t you like that?
I try to be. I think I sometimes watch too much news and it skews my usually-optimistic outlook.

Yeah well I mean you know you have to sort through these issues. But it doesn’t hurt, you know, to kind of know what’s going on too. So for me it’s a kind of a borderline, you know, how much of this do I want to do and how much of that do I want to do. You know if I’m watching TV I like to watch things that I can learn things from, you know, I mean there’s plenty of programs on like that you know, and for me a good day is when I can get up and learn something.
